Commitment.description: A promise between people. `i_owe`: the user promised; `owed_to_me`: someone promised them.
Commitment.title: Commitment

Evidence.description: Where an item came from. Resolves to transcript segments; the quote is optional context.
Evidence.title: Evidence

Gap.description:
A span inside the day that was not recorded, and why. Shown so absence isn't mistaken
for silence.
Gap.title: Gap

Highlight.description: A moment the user marked. User input, so it needs no confidence.
Highlight.title: Highlight

MentionedIn.description: A note whose own words (title or transcript) contain what was asked about.
MentionedIn.title: MentionedIn

Note.description: An idea or an open question.
Note.title: Note

NotePatch.description:
Only the fields present change. An explicit null folder unfiles; a blank title restores
the automatic one.
NotePatch.title: NotePatch

ReportOut.description: The v1 report contract, plus the opted-in transcript lines for `transcript:read`.
ReportOut.title: ReportOut

SyncItemIn.description:
One memory item, mirroring the phone's contract (core `SyncItem`) and the DB CHECK
constraints, so an out-of-contract item is a 422 with a field location — never a 500.
SyncItemIn.title: SyncItemIn

SyncSessionIn.description:
What the phone knows about one session besides its words: the name the person gave it and
exactly when it started. Declaring a session lets the server own it even when no transcript or
item is sent for it (transcript sync off).
SyncSessionIn.title: SyncSessionIn

post.description: Idempotent: unknown, foreign, or already-acknowledged ids are ignored.

put.description:
One key per device token, for the token's lifetime. There is no rotation: a phone that
lost its key has also lost its sealed token (both live behind the Keystore), so it
reconnects with a new token. Refusing rotation means a stolen token can't redirect the
victim's transcripts to a key the thief controls.

get.description: Liveness: the process is up. Says nothing about its dependencies; see /ready.

delete.description:
Deletes the user's server-side data and the user's entire object-storage prefix.

Object storage is cleared before the database cascade; if deletion is incomplete, the
account remains intact so the operation can be retried. The device token is the proof of
possession and is revoked by the same cascading delete.

put.description:
Takes effect for uploads from now on. Every already-received clip keeps the device key
(or lack of one) recorded on it at upload time (ADR-0014): a switch can never expose or
re-seal audio uploaded under an earlier mode's promise, in either direction. No data moves
as part of this call — a mode switch that should also migrate what's already stored
(TODO.md "cloud -> phone: download, verify, then server delete") is not implemented yet.

post.description:
Changes the password and signs every other browser out. Phones keep their tokens: losing
the recorder's connection silently is worse than the risk it removes, and a lost phone is
revoked from the device list instead.

delete.description:
Removes the note, its highlights and transcript from the account, and remembers the id so
the phone, which keeps its own copy, does not send it again.

get.description: Readiness: can this instance serve a request that needs the database?

post.description:
Accepts on-device processed memory from the phone. Idempotent per session.

`deletedSessions` propagates the phone's local deletions (ADR-0020, ADR-0004 amendment):
everything derived from those sessions is removed here too — memory items, report content,
and any server-held clips, transcripts and sealed deliveries. Repeating an id is a no-op.
